subsystems.name: Tensor compute array
subsystems.role: runs the matrix multiplications that dominate neural-network maths.

subsystems.name: On-chip memory hierarchy
subsystems.role: keeps weights and activations as close to the multipliers as possible, because moving data costs far more energy than multiplying it.

subsystems.name: Compression and precision datapath
subsystems.role: shrinks models so they fit in memory and bandwidth budgets.

subsystems.name: System and scheduler
subsystems.role: decides which core — CPU, GPU, NPU — runs each part of a model.

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: turns a trained model into kernels the hardware can execute.

subsystems.name: Off-chip memory interface
subsystems.role: streams model weights and the key-value cache from DRAM when they do not fit on chip.

buildSteps.title: Profile the workload
buildSteps.detail: Measure the shapes and sizes of the matrices actually used on phones — especially token-by-token text generation, which is limited by memory bandwidth rather than raw arithmetic.

buildSteps.title: Choose precision and memory budget
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many bits per weight the hardware must support, and how much SRAM the chip can afford, since these two set both accuracy and unit cost.

buildSteps.title: Design the compute array
buildSteps.detail: Size the array of multiply-accumulate units and its dataflow so that each weight fetched is reused many times before being discarded.

buildSteps.title: Write the register-transfer logic
buildSteps.detail: Describe the datapath, caches and control in a hardware description language, then simulate it against known neural networks.

buildSteps.title: Verify before silicon
buildSteps.detail: Run the design on emulators and field-programmable gate arrays, comparing outputs bit-for-bit with reference software.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and place-and-route
buildSteps.detail: Map the logic onto a leading-edge process node, then lay out transistors and wiring to meet timing within a strict power budget.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and package
buildSteps.detail: The design becomes masks and then wafers in a foundry; the die is packaged alongside CPU, GPU and LPDDR memory in a system-in-package.

buildSteps.title: Bring up driver and runtime
buildSteps.detail: Engineers boot the chip, write firmware and drivers, and validate power, thermals and clock behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Build the compiler and libraries
buildSteps.detail: A graph compiler plus quantisation and operator libraries let developers convert and deploy models without hand-tuning kernels.

prerequisites.why: small geometry is what makes tens of trillions of low-precision operations per second fit in a phone's power and thermal envelope.
cutting weight precision by 4–8× reduces memory traffic, which is the real bottleneck for large language models.
models of a few billion parameters are now small enough to run locally, but with restricted context and quality.
weights and the key-value cache must be streamed from DRAM without draining the battery.
without good compilers, each new model must be hand-optimised for each chip family.

pathway.milestone: NPUs in flagship mobile systems-on-chip, first introduced in 2017 designs such as the Apple A11 Neural Engine and Huawei Kirin 970
pathway.unlocks: private, low-latency inference for vision, speech and small language models.

pathway.milestone: wider low-precision support — INT4 weights, sparsity and compressed key-value caches
pathway.unlocks: larger models running entirely on-device at usable speeds.

pathway.milestone: unified memory across CPU, GPU, NPU and chiplets in laptops and PCs
pathway.unlocks: bigger local models without a discrete accelerator's power cost.

pathway.milestone: personal models that fine-tune and adapt on the device itself
pathway.unlocks: assistants that learn from private data without sending it to a data centre, with cloud used only for hard queries.
